title: Scope the unspoofable peer-attribution comment in delegation_mcp.rs
outcome: delegation_mcp.rs tool_send_to_session (around line 493) says using our own session id is what keeps the attribution unspoofable. That holds for the MCP tool: the calling agent cannot choose the source because the tool hardcodes self.parent_session_id, and the receiving backend resolves it to our display NAME. But the underlying POST /api/sessions/ID/messages route accepts a caller-supplied sourceSessionId, so any local client can set an arbitrary source and spoof attribution. Under the single-user local-only model there is no real attack, but the word unspoofable overstates it system-wide, which is the tm-mdx trap where wrong security-adjacent comments get over-trusted. Fix: scope the wording to unspoofable by the calling agent, or note the raw route trusts sourceSessionId. One-line comment change whenever this file is next touched. Surfaced by review-with-delegate (Claude reviewer); the residual was previously only in the closed tm-5tu reason. The docs under review are correct - they say backend-authoritative.
